scope: Raise Jungle Ruins art quality substantially: unmistakable dirt ground and temple construction assembled from multiple distinct Meshy masonry/block assets, replacing the whole-temple monolith and repeated facade approach. Continue the original foliage, wind, lighting, editor reuse and 60fps objectives.

artDirection.plants: Keep the user's simpler broad leaf geometry and restrained detail. Improve placement, clusters, scale hierarchy and integration.
artDirection.architecture: Modular, dimensioned masonry: separate plain/chipped stones, carved accent blocks, bases/capitals, lintels, roof wedges/cornices and paving slabs. Visible depth, purposeful wear, consistent physical texel scale, few ornamental focal points and authored silhouettes.
artDirection.ground: Dry compacted earth, exposed soil banks and dirt-filled joints. No grassy traversal material. Earth must read as dirt in the live game and editor rebuild.
artDirection.lighting: Warm directional sunlight, cool shaded stone, softer local contact and coherent canopy shade. Evaluate with gameplay framing and neutral asset views.
artDirection.performance: Instance repeated blocks and plants in cullable cells, use bounded texture memory and appropriate LOD, and measure several actual gameplay sections at full render quality.

reviewRequirements: Inspect module silhouettes, bevels, proportions, textures, seams and useful back/side surfaces before assembly.
Compare complete scene compositions against the supplied references, not just an asset thumbnail.
Review the spawn, dirt corridors, pits/log crossing, temple approach, climb, terrace, rooflines and finish.
Preserve authored movement tuning and validate traversal, collisions, checkpoints and finish.
Verify editor reuse, save/reload and the published source version.
Work for at least four additional hours, using the time for construction, art refinement, performance work and review; do not hand off early.
